title: Pediatric arch support: final project documentation
coords: x and y are percent of the page image, measured from the top left
intro: Our 23-page Group 11 report. Page 10 lists contributions; page 16 shows V1 and V2.

hotspots.title: Cover and authors
hotspots.note: Our Group 11 report for BME 3050. Pages 3 to 9 repeat the background review.

hotspots.title: Problem statement
hotspots.note: A positionally adaptable device for growing children aged 5 to 7, with targets of up to 10% volumetric foot growth and a 150 N ground-reaction load. Both are design targets.

hotspots.title: Who did what
hotspots.note: I coordinated clinical contact and researched existing treatments. A teammate fabricated the prototype.

hotspots.title: Work distribution
hotspots.note: My name is on the system diagram, the engineering analysis and the draft V&V matrix. Brainstorming and downselection were done by the team. The effort scores are our own estimates on a 1 to 10 scale.

hotspots.title: Inputs and how we planned to check them
hotspots.note: The table lists six requirements and planned checks. Only the separate dumbbell bench tests have results here.

hotspots.title: V1 and V2
hotspots.note: V1 was cardboard and foam in standard socks: it showed the lift but was not stable. V2 was gel pads in compression sleeves: steadier, and it showed we needed a dedicated pad pocket.

hotspots.title: V2 and V3
hotspots.note: We completed V2. The report calls it a functional alpha; the résumé calls it a beta. V3 remained a hand-off plan.

hotspots.title: Regulatory planning
hotspots.note: The report proposes a classification and submission path. Neither was confirmed through a regulatory review.

hotspots.title: Risk table
hotspots.note: Five failure modes, each with a severity rating and a proposed mitigation.

hotspots.title: Test procedure and pass criterion
hotspots.note: Insert and sleeve on a flat surface, 30 lb dumbbell held on it for 1 minute, then dropped from 1 foot. To pass, no gel outside the pouch, no stitching undone, no fabric torn.

hotspots.title: Results table
hotspots.note: Three static holds and two drops are marked 'Insert Unaffected'. Impact #3 reads: insert slightly damaged, but contained, slight leakage. The report marks that drop as Pass; the design review marks it Fail. Leakage fails the stated criterion.

hotspots.title: Concept sketches
hotspots.note: Three hand-drawn concepts: an oversized insole in a flexible sock, an insole suspended in a non-Newtonian fluid, and an insole with fluid-filled arch bladders. The sock idea is the closest to the sleeve we built.

hotspots.title: Memo to the next team
hotspots.note: The memo hands off the V3 design and proposed testing to a future team.

hotspots.title: TPU printed encasement
hotspots.note: The hand-off memo proposes a 3D-printed TPU casing for the next version. Not built.

hotspots.title: Proposed gait study
hotspots.note: The memo proposes a pediatric gait study to test heel position and fatigue. No pediatric study was run.
